text.arabic_uthmani: ۞ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ أَنتُمُ ٱلْفُقَرَآءُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَٱللَّهُ هُوَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ ٱلْحَمِيدُ

words.gloss_range: vocative particle opening a formal public address

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: vocative support that carries the call toward the definite addressee
definite human collective named as the addressee

words.prose: {{ar:يَٰٓ}} ({{tr:yā}}) opens the ayah as a summons, not as decoration: the poverty claim is heard as direct address before it is processed as doctrine. Its call is formally mediated through {{ar:أَيُّهَا}} ({{tr:ʾayyuhā}}), and the written lengthening lets the address expand audibly before the clause tightens into the human predicate.

topics.headline: formal summons
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that human dependence is delivered as a public call to the hearers, not as a detached proposition about them.
topics.reason: The QAC row and attachment evidence identify a vocative opening, and the CRITICAL rows preserve its scope over the following nominal declaration.

topics.headline: lengthened opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins with an expanded call before the grammar compresses into the identity statement.
topics.reason: The prosodic rows concern the same opening particle and survive as sound-shape payoff rather than as a separate lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: vocative support and alerting particle before the definite addressee

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: opening vocative particle
definite appositive that resolves the addressee

words.prose: {{ar:أَيُّهَا}} ({{tr:ʾayyuhā}}) is the bridge that lets the call reach the definite human class. It holds the address open until {{ar:ٱلنَّاسُ}} ({{tr:an-nāsu}}) names the audience, so the ayah stages attention before it states dependence.

topics.headline: definite-address bridge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the definite human class is not called abruptly; the grammar supplies a formal bridge into public address.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the support frame and following apposition syntactically licensed.

topics.headline: alerted staging
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices attention itself becoming part of the utterance before humanity is named.
topics.reason: The rows converge on the support word as both formal connector and alerting element within the address unit.

words.gloss_range: definite human collective named in apposition to the vocative frame
words.root_gloss_range: human social presence, familiarity, and perception remain relevant as root pressure, while the local surface functions as the known human class

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: second-person plural pronoun resuming the named audience
predicate that redefines the human collective by need

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلنَّاسُ}} ({{tr:an-nāsu}}) completes the vocative as the known human class, not a tribe or subset. The following {{ar:أَنتُمُ}} ({{tr:antumu}}) turns that public category into direct second person within the surah's repeated human-address thread (35:3, 35:5, 35:28, 35:45), and the root field of social presence makes the point sharper: even the socially perceptive human collective is named only to be redefined as needy.

topics.headline: universal addressee
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the claim of need is aimed at humanity as a public class, not at a limited social group.
topics.reason: The local apposition and definite collective noun support a species-wide addressee.

topics.headline: social human pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an irony: the creature named through social presence and recognition still needs to be told its dependence.
topics.reason: The root derivation pressure is useful, but the local form remains the conventional human collective rather than activating every disputed derivation.

topics.headline: category becomes you
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the audience move from named public category to direct accountability, within the surah's repeated human-address thread (35:3, 35:5, 35:28, 35:45).
topics.reason: The local pronoun reprise is strongly licensed, and the cited same-surah rows give concrete public-address parallels.

words.gloss_range: independent second-person plural pronoun as overt nominal subject

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: named addressee resumed by the pronoun
predicate assigned to the addressees

words.prose: {{ar:أَنتُمُ}} ({{tr:antumu}}) makes the audience grammatically visible. The address does not leave humanity as a category at a distance: the plural pronoun places the hearers under the predicate {{ar:ٱلْفُقَرَآءُ}} ({{tr:al-fuqarāʾu}}), in a verbless clause that reads as a standing identity rather than a passing event.

topics.headline: overt addressed subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the universal noun become a direct you, so the dependence claim cannot remain abstract.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence resumes the vocative audience, and the independent pronoun supplies an overt nominal subject.

topics.headline: plural standing identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plural address distributes the predicate across the whole audience and presents it as a stable nominal relation.
topics.reason: The pronoun-predicate attachment is strongly licensed, and no local evidence narrows the plural public address to male-only reference.

words.gloss_range: definite broken plural predicate naming humans as the needy ones, completed by a directional complement toward God
words.root_gloss_range: need, poverty, dependence, gaps, piercing, and broken-support imagery; local grammar selects creaturely dependence rather than merely economic poverty

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: subject of the predicate
prepositional complement directing the need toward God
opposite divine predicate answering human need

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْفُقَرَآءُ}} ({{tr:al-fuqarāʾu}}) is the predicate of {{ar:أَنتُمُ}} ({{tr:antumu}}), so the clause identifies humans by need rather than narrating their becoming poor. The complement {{ar:إِلَى ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:ilā Allāhi}}) prevents a merely economic reading: the root's images of gap, fracture, and lack are narrowed into creaturely dependence directed to God, and the next clause answers that lack with {{ar:ٱلْغَنِىُّ}} ({{tr:al-ghaniyyu}}), the same poverty-sufficiency polarity seen in reversed order at 47:38.

topics.headline: categorical poverty predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that poverty is assigned as a defining predicate for the addressed humans, not as a temporary economic episode.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the word as predicate of the second-person subject, while the definite broken plural supports a classifying force.

topics.headline: need directed to God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the predicate is completed by a direction: human lack points toward God rather than toward created patrons.
topics.reason: The prepositional complement is syntactically forced and aligns with the V4 dependence-on-God branch.

topics.headline: broken-support image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that need is pictured as lack of support from within, while the local phrase keeps dependence on God as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The broader root family supplies fracture and hollowing images, but the local adjective plus complement selects needful dependence rather than a literal wound, pit, calamity, or mount-loan sense.

topics.headline: poverty answered by sufficiency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that human poverty is defined against divine needlessness, with the same polarity appearing in a reversed order at 47:38.
topics.reason: The two predicates form the ayah's main contrast, and the supplied 47:38 evidence supports the cross-ayah polarity without overriding the local order.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the endpoint and direction of need

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: predicate completed by the prepositional phrase
genitive object governed by the preposition

words.prose: {{ar:إِلَى}} ({{tr:ilā}}) turns the poverty predicate into an oriented relation. It governs {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) and makes the endpoint of human need visible after the lack has first been named.

topics.headline: governed endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that need is not left open-ended; the preposition points it to its divine endpoint.
topics.reason: The attachment table marks the following divine name as the governed complement of this preposition.

topics.headline: delayed orientation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sequence first land on lack, then reveal where that lack tends.
topics.reason: The rows describe the local ordering and recited transition from the predicate into the prepositional complement.

words.gloss_range: genitive proper divine name as the endpoint of human need
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine name with worship, refuge, awe, and orientation pressures; local grammar keeps it as the named endpoint, not a generic divine category

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition governing the divine name
same name repeated as nominative subject in the next clause

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) names the endpoint of dependence as the proper divine name, not as a generic sacred category; its worship, refuge, awe, and longing pressures fit the movement of need toward God without replacing the proper-name role. Its genitive case places it inside the human-need clause, but the same name immediately returns as {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}), so the endpoint of need becomes the subject of sufficiency across the clause boundary.

topics.headline: named endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that human dependence is directed to God by name, not to a vague category of sacred power.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the proper name as genitive complement, and contextual evidence marks the referent as God.

topics.headline: worship-refuge pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the endpoint of need carries worship, refuge, awe, and longing pressures, while the local form remains the proper divine name.
topics.reason: No V4 root rows are present for this root, so the derivational pressure can color orientation but cannot replace the local proper-name role.

topics.headline: case pivot echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same divine name close the first clause as endpoint and reopen the second clause as subject.
topics.reason: The repeated name with changed case is a local formal echo that supports the ayah's clause pivot.

words.gloss_range: conjunction opening the contrastive second nominal clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: clause-ending divine name before the pivot
repeated divine name beginning the second clause

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins two complete nominal clauses and, because the predicates are opposites, carries a whereas-force without turning the second clause into a subordinate explanation. Bound to {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}), it audibly restarts the clause by making the endpoint of need the new subject.

topics.headline: coordinated contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices two complete states placed side by side: humans are needy while God is need-free.
topics.reason: The attachment constraints treat the second nominal clause as contrastive and complete.

topics.headline: clause pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the conjunction fused to the repeated name, turning continuity into a fresh grammatical start.
topics.reason: The rows focus on the proclitic form and the local shift from the first divine-name role into the second.

words.gloss_range: nominative proper divine name as subject of the second nominal clause
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine name with worship/refuge orientation pressures; locally the same named referent shifts from endpoint to subject

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: same name in genitive endpoint role
separator pronoun and two predicates attached to the subject
first predicate in the divine title pair
second predicate in the divine title pair

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) repeats the same name that just stood after the preposition, but now nominative as the subject of the second clause. The repetition refuses a thin pronominal shortcut: the named endpoint of human dependence is explicitly the bearer of {{ar:ٱلْغَنِىُّ}} ({{tr:al-ghaniyyu}}) and {{ar:ٱلْحَمِيدُ}} ({{tr:al-ḥamīdu}}), while 47:38 shows the same polarity with God named first.

topics.headline: repeated nominative subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same name regain grammatical independence as subject rather than being resumed by a pronoun.
topics.reason: The QAC grammar and attachment table identify this occurrence as the nominative subject of the second nominal clause.

topics.headline: attributes anchored to name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that sufficiency and praiseworthiness attach to the named God, not to a vague divine abstraction.
topics.reason: Both closing predicates are attached to this subject in the local syntax.

topics.headline: endpoint becomes subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the central reversal: the one toward whom need points becomes the one from whom needlessness is asserted, with the same polarity also visible at 47:38.
topics.reason: The role reversal is local and concrete; root-derivation claims are kept as pressure, not as replacement for the proper-name subject.

words.gloss_range: independent third-person singular pronoun functioning as separator and emphatic hinge before the predicates

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: subject resumed and emphasized by the pronoun
definite predicate pair clarified by the separator

words.prose: {{ar:هُوَ}} ({{tr:huwa}}) stands between the definite subject and the definite predicate pair, clarifying predication and giving divine identity a visible beat before the titles. It does not introduce another referent; it routes both closing predicates back to {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) and thickens the second clause against the shorter human clause.

topics.headline: separator pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the titles are asserted of the named subject, not read as loose modifiers or a separate referent.
topics.reason: The attachment constraints describe the pronoun as separating and emphatic after the divine name.

topics.headline: emphatic buffer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a compact pause that intensifies the contrast before the two divine titles arrive.
topics.reason: The independent pronoun is locally coherent as a visible and rhythmic reinforcement before the predicate pair.

words.gloss_range: definite divine predicate naming intrinsic freedom from need
words.root_gloss_range: sufficiency, wealth, availing, enriching, claimed independence, song, dwelling, and other branches; local grammar and contrast select lacklessness, not ordinary wealth or unrelated branches

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: human predicate answered by the divine opposite
separator before the predicate title
second title completing the closing pair
divine subject of the predicate title

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْغَنِىُّ}} ({{tr:al-ghaniyyu}}) is the first closing predicate, asserted of {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) after the separator. Against {{ar:ٱلْفُقَرَآءُ}} ({{tr:al-fuqarāʾu}}), it means not ordinary wealth but intrinsic freedom from need; the broader root range of enriching or claimed independence is narrowed into the title's stable lacklessness before {{ar:ٱلْحَمِيدُ}} ({{tr:al-ḥamīdu}}) adds praise. The same title works as part of the recurring divine pair and polarity in 31:26, 14:8, and 47:38.

topics.headline: definite need-free title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that God is named as the need-free one, directly answering the human predicate rather than merely being richer.
topics.reason: The local predicate slot and opposition to human need select divine lacklessness.

topics.headline: sufficiency root range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices stable intrinsic sufficiency, while enriching others and claimed self-sufficiency remain contrastive pressures rather than the local surface sense.
topics.reason: The V4 branches are broad, but the definite predicate adjective after the divine subject licenses the needlessness branch and narrows other branches to background contrast.

topics.headline: formulaic antithesis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the title functioning both as the opposite of human poverty and as part of a recurring divine title pair (31:26, 14:8, 47:38).
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows give concrete parallels for the same attribute pair or polarity, while the local clause determines the order and contrast.

topics.headline: first closing predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah resolves need through sufficiency before sealing the contrast with praise.
topics.reason: The predicate order places this title before the final praise title, and the sound-form rows add local cadence without changing sense.

words.gloss_range: definite divine predicate naming intrinsic praiseworthiness
words.root_gloss_range: praise, commendation, recognized excellence, praiseworthy quality, and related praise-seeking or intensive branches; local title selects inherent praiseworthiness, not a posture of seeking praise

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: first predicate paired with the final title
subject of the predicate pair

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْحَمِيدُ}} ({{tr:al-ḥamīdu}}) is a second predicate of {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}), not an ornamental tag after {{ar:ٱلْغَنِىُّ}} ({{tr:al-ghaniyyu}}). It turns divine sufficiency into recognized excellence: the one who has no need is also intrinsically praiseworthy, and the final word folds the dependence claim back into the surah's praise frame (35:1, 35:34) while preserving the recurrent title pair seen in 14:8 and 31:26.

topics.headline: second asserted predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that praise is a full asserted title beside sufficiency, not a loose afterthought.
topics.reason: The attachment table identifies the word as a second predicate of the divine subject.

topics.headline: inherent praiseworthiness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices praiseworthiness as an intrinsic attribute, while praise-seeking and one-time praising are excluded by the local title.
topics.reason: The broader praise root includes several branches, but the definite title in the divine predicate slot selects objective praiseworthiness.

topics.headline: evaluative close
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not end on human lack but on divine worth.
topics.reason: The rows consistently treat the final title as the semantic and auditory landing of the ayah.

topics.headline: praise-thread echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final title reconnecting the human-dependence argument to the surah's praise thread and to the title pair's recurrence (14:8, 31:26, 35:1, 35:34).
topics.reason: The supplied references give concrete inter-ayah links while the local final position determines the payoff.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The identity clause addresses all people, identifies them as the needy, and directs that need toward God before reversing the relation with the independent and praiseworthy God.
baseline_models.mechanism: The definite human collective is identified with directed need rather than merely compared with a richer party. The repeated divine name and independent pronoun make the relation asymmetric: humanity faces toward a source it cannot reciprocally supply, while praise marks that asymmetry as worthy rather than arbitrary.

activation_trace.role: The visibly human collective, contrasted with wild solitude, supplies the universally addressed species rather than a poor subgroup.
Need and lack supply the clause's explicit dependent condition.
The worshipped one supplies the personal terminus of the directed need and excludes an impersonal abstraction.
Independence from need supplies the opposite pole of the relation.
Praise opposed to blame makes the asymmetry evaluative, not merely quantitative.

changed_reading.before: A comparison between economically poor people and a rich deity.
changed_reading.after: A universal relational claim: humanity as humanity is need directed toward God, while God alone is independent and worthy of praise.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The pairing of the needy with al-Ghani and al-Hamid permits the active sufficiency branch of ghina to connect the two halves.
baseline_models.mechanism: Divine non-need is not sterile self-enclosure. The sufficiency branch of ghina includes being enough for another and standing in for what that other lacks; al-Hamid then names the quality of that effective sufficiency.

activation_trace.role: Human lack creates the relational demand that sufficiency answers.
Effective enoughness that benefits or substitutes for another turns divine independence outward toward the needy.
Abundant praiseworthy qualities characterize the sufficiency as beneficent rather than inert.

changed_reading.after: God needs nothing and is enough for those who need; the praise follows from sufficiency that actually answers lack.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The focus noun for poverty carries branches of vertebral articulation, lending a back, and a calamity that breaks the back.
baseline_models.mechanism: Human need can be imaged as an articulated load-bearing structure: segmented, able to lend support, yet vulnerable to a load that breaks it. Direction toward God then resembles reliance by a structure that does not hold itself together absolutely.

activation_trace.role: Jointed vertebrae give poverty an anatomical structure of connected but non-self-supporting parts.
Making a back available for another supplies a social mechanism of borrowed carrying capacity.
A back-breaking calamity exposes the limit of creaturely support.

changed_reading.after: Poverty can also name structural load-bearing vulnerability: humans are articulated supports whose backs can be lent and broken.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Branches of the focus poverty root include an earthen outlet or pit and a cut or perforation, while the preposition directs need toward God.
baseline_models.mechanism: Need can be carried as an opening rather than only an absence. A pit, outlet, cut, or perforation makes the human subject receptive but unable to determine what enters or fills it; divine enoughness names the adequate source.

activation_trace.role: An earthen pit or outlet gives need a receptive spatial form.
A cut or perforation sharpens receptivity into an exposed passage.
Enoughness supplies what the receptive opening cannot produce for itself.

changed_reading.before: Need is a static deficit possessed by people.
changed_reading.after: Need is also an exposed, directed receptivity whose filling depends on God.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: A focus branch distinguishes poverty of the self produced by greed and lack of contentment from external want.
baseline_models.mechanism: The universal address can include affluent people because poverty has an affective mode: appetite continually manufactures lack. Divine independence supplies a countercondition not governed by acquisition or craving.

activation_trace.role: Greedy, uncontented poverty of the self supplies an inward form of need that wealth does not remove.
Independence from need contrasts with appetite's endless production of new wants.
Praise locates worth outside the appetite-and-acquisition cycle.

changed_reading.before: Only those without possessions are poor.
changed_reading.after: Every person remains needy, and one plausible layer diagnoses the especially deep poverty created by uncontented appetite.

context_deltas.mechanism: The aperture baseline becomes a controlled circulation model. Mercy is opened, held, and released, while provision is allotted to humanity; need is therefore not only a hole but dependence on channels whose access and flow no creature controls independently.

activation_trace.role: The focus pit or outlet supplies the receiving end of the circulation.
The focus perforation supplies a passage whose exposure does not grant control over inflow.
Divine enoughness supplies the adequate source at the other end of the channel.
An opened closure and widened entrance give the channel an access mechanism.
Water issuing from an outlet turns opening into a concrete image of released flow.
Merciful tenderness names what moves through the opened channel.
Grasping and confinement supply the valve-like possibility of withholding flow.
Sending and setting in motion supply release after restraint.
An allotted gift turns general flow into provision assigned to dependent recipients.

structural_cues: 35:2 arranges mercy inside a reversible open, hold, and release sequence; 35:3 repeats the address to humanity and asks who provisions it from above and below.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies aperture, retention, release, mercy, and allotted provision; I infer that these flows provide mechanics for the focus direction toward God. They could instead remain separate examples of sovereignty without redescribing poverty.

changed_reading.before: Human need is a static emptiness facing divine abundance.
changed_reading.after: Human need depends on opened channels of mercy and provision whose inflow, withholding, and release belong to God alone.

context_deltas.mechanism: The dead land provides a material analogy for the needy human: unable to revive itself yet capable of receiving a transported, life-making flow. Poverty becomes receptive potential within an ecological chain rather than pure negation.

activation_trace.role: The earthen opening in the focus root makes human need materially comparable to receptive ground.
Enoughness supplies a source capable of making receptive lack fruitful.
Sending initiates the ecological delivery chain.
Wind and moving air provide the carrier that the receiving land does not command.
A drawn-along cloud supplies the transported reservoir.
Driving something onward supplies direction from source to needy destination.
Lifeless land supplies the extreme case of a recipient unable to activate itself.
Dry growth revived by rain makes reception visibly productive and lets the resurrection endpoint retain its ecological texture.

structural_cues: 35:9 forms a causal sequence from sending wind to moving cloud to dead country to revived earth, then names resurrection as the analogue.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a transported flow, inert land, and revival; I infer that the chain materializes the focus relation of need and sufficiency. The live alternative is that the chain concerns resurrection alone and only secondarily illuminates human poverty.

changed_reading.after: Poverty can be receptive creaturely potential: like dead land, humanity cannot self-quicken but can become fruitful through a delivered divine flow.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same dust inventory supplies opposed social images, poverty through clinging to dust and wealth through abundance of soil, while 35:11 makes dust humanity's common origin. The focus contrast therefore cannot be reduced to two stable possession classes: created dependence precedes both scarcity and abundance.

activation_trace.role: Ordinary need supplies the apparent poor side of the focus contrast.
Independence supplies the apparent rich side of the focus contrast.
Poverty imaged as sticking to dust joins the human origin material to low possession status.
Wealth imaged as abundant soil makes the identical origin material support the opposite possession status.

structural_cues: 35:11 predicates creation from one material before differentiating pairing, gestation, and measured lifetimes.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a common dust origin and opposed poverty and wealth branches within that root; I infer that social status is secondary to creaturely dependence. The branches may instead be lexical alternatives with no intended simultaneous activation.

changed_reading.before: The focus divides a poor human class from a rich divine party.
changed_reading.after: All humans arise from a substrate capable of imaging both poverty and wealth, so no amount of creaturely abundance exits the shared condition of dependence.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus direction toward God becomes exclusive rather than generically devotional. Proposed substitutes possess not even a seed's thin covering and cannot hear or answer; they cannot own the smallest resource or complete the response loop required by need.

activation_trace.role: The worshipped one anchors the focus direction in a specific divine recipient.
Effective sufficiency sets the capacity a true recipient of need must possess.
Ownership and power of disposal supply the capacity explicitly denied to alternative recipients.
Otherness marks the proposed substitutes as recipients apart from God.
The seed's thin covering supplies a deliberately minimal ownership test that the substitutes fail.
Auditory reception supplies the first half of a response loop that the substitutes lack.
Returning an answer supplies the second half of the failed response loop.

structural_cues: 35:13-14 descends from cosmic rule to ownership of a minute covering, then tests hearing and answering in sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies non-ownership, non-hearing, and non-response; I infer that these failures specify why the focus preposition terminates at God. The narrower alternative is a polemic against particular invoked beings rather than a general account of dependency.

changed_reading.before: People happen to direct their need toward God.
changed_reading.after: Need is directed exclusively toward God because every proposed substitute fails both the smallest ownership test and the basic hear-and-answer relation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The universal human collective is dependent not only for goods but for its continued occupancy of creation. The conditional removal of present humanity and arrival of a newly originated creation makes human non-necessity explicit while divine independence remains unaffected.

activation_trace.role: The whole human collective supplies what can be removed rather than merely deprived of goods.
Need expands from lacking resources to lacking necessity of existence.
Divine independence remains stable across removal and replacement.
Departure and passing away provide the removal side of creaturely contingency.
Arrival supplies replacement after removal.
Origination makes the replacement a newly created collective rather than a rearrangement of human assets.
New occurrence after a break makes discontinuity between populations explicit.

structural_cues: 35:16 is a compact conditional with present humanity as the removable object and a new creation as its replacement.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies removal, arrival, origination, and newness; I infer that these recast poverty as contingency and replaceability. The alternative is to hear only a threat of punishment without drawing an ontological conclusion.

changed_reading.before: Humans exist securely but depend on God for what they possess.
changed_reading.after: Humanity depends on God even for continued existence and is not necessary to the independent God, who can originate another collective.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus back imagery meets a laden person whose heavy burden cannot be carried by another. Universal poverty therefore does not pool persons into one interchangeable deficit: social backs may be lent in ordinary life, but ultimate moral load remains individually nontransferable.

activation_trace.role: Vertebral articulation supplies the bodily frame on which a burden would rest.
Lending a back supplies the plausible but here limited mechanism of interpersonal substitution.
A back-breaking event supplies the point at which ordinary support fails.
A heavy burden supplies the moral load repeatedly denied transfer.
Weight opposed to lightness intensifies the load borne by the calling person.
Bearing a trust or culpable load specifies the carrying action no other person performs.

structural_cues: 35:18 repeats burden and carrying forms, stages a call for help, and denies transfer even when kinship is present.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies vertebrae, back-lending, heaviness, and refused carrying; I infer a bodily geometry for individual accountability. The alternative is that the anatomical focus branches remain dormant and the burden language is purely juridical.

changed_reading.before: Shared human poverty might imply that one person's support can finally substitute for another's.
changed_reading.after: All people share dependence, yet each remains a distinct bearer: no borrowed back transfers the ultimate moral load.

context_deltas.mechanism: Needy recipients spend out of prior allotment, an outflow that could look like depletion, but the sequence names it commerce protected from stagnation and completed by full payment, growth, and gifted surplus. Dependence becomes participatory circulation rather than anxious hoarding.

activation_trace.role: Human lack makes spending materially paradoxical rather than effortless disposal of surplus.
Enoughness supports a return economy that does not depend on extracting resources from the poor giver.
Money going out in expenditure supplies the giver's real release of held resources.
Exhaustion and disappearance preserve the felt risk that outflow could deplete a needy giver.
Allotted gift marks what is spent as prior provision rather than autonomous ownership.
Trade seeking gain turns expenditure into expected relational return.
Stagnation until spoilage names the market failure explicitly excluded from this trade.
Completion without shortfall supplies the promised settlement.
Growth beyond completion supplies increase rather than mere replacement.
Gifted beneficence makes the increase grace rather than a resource extracted from God by contract.

structural_cues: 35:29 constrains spending as coming from prior provision and names a hoped-for trade; 35:30 completes the purpose with full payment and additional bounty.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies prior allotment, real outflow, commerce, non-stagnation, full return, and increase; I infer a circulation model in which acknowledged poverty enables generosity. The alternative is to keep the commercial language only as reward metaphor.

changed_reading.before: Being poor toward God encourages preservation of every scarce possession.
changed_reading.after: Recognized dependence permits spending from received provision: the poor can release resources because divine sufficiency completes and exceeds the return.

context_deltas.mechanism: Al-Hamid becomes experientially testable rather than a decorative title. Later speakers praise after grief is removed and after gifted emplacement in a lasting dwelling where exhausting labor no longer reaches them; praise is the retrospective recognition of sufficiency encountered.

activation_trace.role: Effective enoughness supplies the benefit later experienced as relief and rest.
Finding someone or something praiseworthy after experience makes the focus title open to later verification.
Uttered praise after an experienced change realizes the focus title in the recipients' voice.
The roughness of inward grief supplies the prior condition that sufficient relief removes.
Settling in a place supplies durable emplacement after need.
Belonging to or residing in a dwelling gives the relief a stable social location.
Beneficent gift identifies the source of the dwelling as grace rather than self-provision.
Wearisome affliction supplies one form of insufficiency excluded from the settled state.
Weakness and fatigue supply the second form of insufficiency excluded from the settled state.

structural_cues: 35:34 gives praise after removal of grief, and 35:35 immediately explains the lasting dwelling, its gifted source, and the absence of two kinds of exhaustion.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies praise after relief, gifted emplacement, and ended fatigue; I infer that these narratively test the focus pairing of sufficiency and praiseworthiness. The alternative is that the later praise remains a separate eschatological scene.

changed_reading.before: Al-Hamid is a conventional honorific appended to divine self-sufficiency.
changed_reading.after: God is found praiseworthy when divine enoughness is experienced as grief removed, grace-given dwelling, and exhaustion ended.

context_deltas.mechanism: The inward poverty of greed gains an accountable location. The breasts are not just containers but an origin from which actions issue, and their hidden contents are known; appetite-driven lack can therefore generate conduct even when external wealth conceals it.

activation_trace.role: Greedy poverty of the self supplies the concealed appetite under examination.
Independence from need supplies the countercondition to appetite-generated lack.
Disclosure to the knower makes concealed appetite available to divine knowledge.
An inner source from which actions proceed turns appetite into a causal origin rather than a private feeling.

structural_cues: 35:38 moves from knowledge of the unseen cosmos to intimate knowledge of what belongs to breasts.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies inward greed, disclosed hidden content, and an origin of actions; I infer that one form of focus poverty is an appetite that drives conduct. The alternative is that knowledge of breasts is general and does not particularly activate greed.

changed_reading.before: Poverty names an externally visible shortage.
changed_reading.after: One live reading locates poverty in hidden appetite that issues into action and remains known even beneath outward abundance.

context_deltas.mechanism: Human dependence is nested in a larger maintained order. Heaven and earth can leave their state unless held, and no successor can hold them afterward; need is therefore continuous suspension and preservation, not only an original act of creation or an occasional request.

activation_trace.role: Articulated structural dependence supplies a focus-scale image for an order requiring support.
Independence identifies the holder as outside the instability being maintained.
Holding and confining supply the ongoing support that prevents cosmic departure.
Leaving a place or state supplies the instability continually prevented by that holding.

structural_cues: 35:41 repeats both holding and leaving, then denies any holder after God if the heavens and earth should leave their state.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies cosmic instability, continuous holding, and the absence of a replacement holder; I infer that this is the large-scale mechanics of focus poverty. It could instead remain a cosmological proof without redefining human need.

changed_reading.before: Humans needed God at creation and in moments of shortage.
changed_reading.after: Creaturely need is continuous maintenance within an upheld cosmos; dependence persists at every moment of apparent stability.

context_deltas.mechanism: An anomalous focus branch places control and strength inside the poverty root, and 35:44 recalls people of greater gathered force who still could not make God fail. Human poverty therefore need not erase real power or agency; it marks the limit and derivation of that power.

activation_trace.role: Control and strength over an affair preserve genuine creaturely capacity inside the lexical field of poverty.
Need prevents real capacity from becoming independence.
Divine independence supplies the kind of non-derivative power humans never reach.
Force gathered like strands supplies the strongest human counterexample to equating poverty with weakness.
Failure or incapacity supplies the condition human strength cannot impose on God.
Effective power that reaches action and possession supplies the final divine contrast.

structural_cues: 35:44 explicitly compares earlier peoples as stronger, then denies that anything can incapacitate God and closes with knowledge and power.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a strength branch within the focus root and a comparative-strength scene that still fails against God; I infer that dependence is compatible with consequential human agency. The focus branch may instead be lexically isolated and inactive here.

changed_reading.before: Calling humans poor means they have no real strength or agency.
changed_reading.after: Humans may possess formidable, gathered strength and still be poor toward God because capacity is limited and never makes God dependent or incapable.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the place-and-dwelling branch of ghina is form-distant from ordinary divine self-sufficiency. It remains anchored in the focus epithet and is activated by the later grammar of settling in a gifted permanent dwelling without fatigue. Downstream prose should present it only as a spatial resonance of sufficiency, not translate al-Ghani as a house or claim that 35:35 directly glosses 35:15.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Al-Ghani at focus word 9 carries a branch of residence and long dwelling opposite the directed unsettledness of human need.

activation_trace.role: Residence and long dwelling give divine sufficiency a form-distant spatial possibility.
Human need supplies the unsettled condition seeking adequate emplacement.
Settling in a place activates the latent spatial side of sufficiency.
Residence and belonging to a dwelling make emplacement durable.
The absence of wearing toil marks the dwelling as sufficient rather than another site of extraction.
The absence of fatigue completes the image of settled enoughness.

changed_reading.before: Richness is possession of an inventory.
changed_reading.after: As a contained spatial resonance, divine sufficiency can be imagined as stable emplacement that settles the needy and ends exhausting displacement.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the human image in the pupil is a remote branch reached through the packet's mapping of the people root. It remains anchored in the exact focus address and gains a closing cue when God is described as seeing the servants. Downstream prose must call it an optical metaphor for being seen, never attribute a bodily pupil to God or present it as the lexical meaning of al-nas.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus address to people carries a branch in which the human figure appears as an image in the eye's dark center.

activation_trace.role: The human figure reflected in the pupil turns the addressed collective into a possible image of visible persons.
The repeated people-root near the close carries the same optical branch into the final accountability scene.
Actual seeing supplies the contextual activation that turns the pupil image into a contained visibility metaphor.

changed_reading.before: The people are an anonymous mass told that it is needy.
changed_reading.after: In a cautious optical overlay, the needy collective consists of visible persons held within divine sight rather than an unseen abstraction.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the focus praise root's branch of soliciting credit for favors contrastively rather than as the direct sense of al-Hamid. It remains anchored because independence immediately precedes praise, while later forbearance and delayed collection separate divine action from urgent repayment. Downstream prose should frame it as a rejected praise economy, not assert that the epithet itself means refusing thanks.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The immediate pairing of al-Ghani with al-Hamid can negate the branch in which a benefactor reminds recipients of favors in order to extract praise.

activation_trace.role: Seeking praise by rehearsing one's favors supplies the needy credit economy placed under contrast.
Independence from need blocks any requirement for reputational payment from beneficiaries.
Deliberate restraint supplies a divine posture not driven by urgent collection.
Acquired gain supplies the human earnings on which consequences could be collected.
Letting go or leaving supplies the counterfactual restraint from immediate total seizure.

changed_reading.before: God is praised, which could be imagined as praise owed back to a benefactor who needs recognition.
changed_reading.after: As a contained contrast, the independent God does not extract praise as reputational repayment; praise answers beneficence freely joined to forbearance.

strongest_changes: Static poverty became directed circulation: opened mercy, allotted provision, ecological delivery, and divine enoughness describe how need is answered.
Dust carrying both poverty and wealth displaced a simple class contrast with a shared created condition prior to either scarcity or abundance.
Universal dependence remained compatible with individual accountability and real human strength: burdens do not transfer, yet power never becomes independence.
Divine sufficiency became continuous and experiential through non-failing return, relief, durable rest, and the ongoing holding of a potentially unstable cosmos.
summary.what_was_special: The focus inventories generated several concrete geometries of need: aperture, articulated back, hidden appetite, circulating expenditure, and unstable emplacement. Context did not collapse them into one explanation; it activated distinct causal models and preserved the form-distant dust, dwelling, sight, and praise-economy readings with explicit containment.
remaining_uncertainties: The anatomical, perforation, dwelling, and pupil branches may be live resonances or only useful abductive analogies rather than intended lexical senses.
The opposed poverty and wealth branches of dust may legitimately coexist here, but they may also remain separate idiomatic developments.
The extent to which later experienced praise explains al-Hamid, rather than merely exemplifying praise in another scene, remains open.
Continuous ontological dependence, moral nontransferability, and consequential human agency coexist in the trace without a final hierarchy among them.

baseline.text: Ey insanlar, Allah'a muhtaç olan sizsiniz. Allah ise hiçbir şeye muhtaç değildir ve övgüye layıktır.

findings.text: İnsanın ihtiyacı, kendi kendini taşıyamayan bir omurga gibi, varoluşu ayakta tutan yapısal ve yönelmiş bir bağımlılıktır.
Allah'ın övgüye layık oluşu, bir karşılığa ihtiyaç duymasından değil, tam yeterlilikten bağımlılara akan iyiliğin tanınmasından doğar.

inter_ayah_rows.note: It repeats the full declaration that God is self-sufficient and praiseworthy, while explaining that human withholding harms only the withholder.

inter_ayah_rows.label: no value
inter_ayah_rows.note: The rejection of worshipping other than God does not specifically clarify human poverty or divine self-sufficiency.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It directly reverses the false claim that God is poor and people are rich, exposing the focus ayah's actual dependence relation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: God's ownership of all that is in heaven and earth is joined directly to His self-sufficiency and praise-worthiness.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The immediate continuation shows that people can be removed and replaced, concretizing their contingency before God.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It states that universal human disbelief does not diminish God, who remains self-sufficient and praiseworthy.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It pairs God's ownership of heaven and earth with the exact declaration of His self-sufficiency and praise-worthiness.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The nearby signs of rain and varied produce display provision flowing from God to a dependent world.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Musa explicitly confesses his need for whatever good God sends, giving a concrete human instance of directed poverty.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It directly contrasts God's self-sufficiency with human poverty and shows that withholding rebounds upon the self.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The immediate continuation affirms that replacing people is not difficult for God, reinforcing their non-necessity to Him.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its portrayal of a person claiming self-sufficiency supplies a contrasting human posture to the focus ayah's universal poverty.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It repeats that turning away leaves God self-sufficient and praiseworthy, not dependent on human response.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The nearby description of prayer and spending from what God provided presents human action as drawing on received provision.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It shows that wealth and children cannot make their possessors sufficient before God.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It identifies real but concealed human poverty and calls for attentive support rather than judging by apparent self-sufficiency.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Need is answered through capacity, circulating trade, expenditure, and a return that is complete rather than depleted.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Spiritual dependence is rendered as appetite, market liquidity, bid competition, payroll, and settlement of an account.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Need, appetite, and sufficiency
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Material lack or an unbounded appetite creates dependence, while sufficient means allow an agent to stand without that need.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: material need and poverty (quranic:root_001169:B002/m01); appetite-driven poverty of the self (quranic:root_001169:B004/m01); wealth and independence (quranic:root_001110:B001/m01); sufficiency that stands in for another resource (quranic:root_001110:B002/m01); fortune or worldly means (quranic:root_000227:B002/m01)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Poverty is split into external lack and internal appetite, while wealth is split into possession and functional sufficiency. The contrast clarifies that abundance can fail to remove dependence when desire itself remains unbounded.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi görmeyi temel alır, fakat belirli kullanımlarda işitmeyi, bir belirtiyi anlayıp ayırt etmeyi ve çevreye bakarak birini aramayı da aynı dalda aktarır. identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal duyusal olarak fark etmeyi ve belirtilen bağlamlardaki işitme, sezme ve bakıp araştırma kullanımlarını kapsar; yakınlık ve rahatlık duygusunu kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Görüp fark etme çekirdeği ile ses işitme, olgunluk belirtisini ayırt etme ve çevreye bakıp araştırma kalıpları ayrı tutulur; kalıplardaki kapsam çıplak biçime genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi görüp fark etmeyi anlatır. Belirli kullanımlarda bir sesi işitmeye, bir kimsedeki olgunluk belirtisini ya da kaygı veren bir durumu sezmeye ve çevreye bakarak birinin bulunup bulunmadığını araştırmaya uzanır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyi gözle görerek fark etmeyi veya seçmeyi anlatır.
Belirli bir ses nesnesiyle kullanıldığında o sesi işitmeyi anlatır.
Bir kimsedeki olgunluk belirtisini bilip ayırt etmeyi veya kaygı veren bir durumu duyularla sezmeyi anlatabilir.
Çevreye bakıp dikkatle araştırarak birinin bulunup bulunmadığını anlamaya çalışma kullanımını taşır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Aktarılan anlam alanının merkezi görüp fark etmektir. Aynı ifade ailesi belirli nesne ve yapılarda işitme, bir belirtiyi anlayıp ayırt etme, kaygı veren şeyi sezme ve bakıp araştırma yönlerinde kullanılır; bunlar sınırsız bir genel algı anlamı oluşturmaz.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir kişi veya şey karşısında yabancılık ve ürkme duygusunun kalkmasını çekirdek anlam olarak verir. Yakınlık ve sevinç, rahatlık veren kişi ya da şey ve insana alışık saldırgan olmayan hayvan kullanımları bu çekirdekten bağımlı biçimde açıklanabilir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal duygusal yakınlık, rahatlık ve bunları sağlayan varlıkları kapsar; insan türünün adı, duyusal fark etme ve insana bakan yan anlamları dışarıda kalır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yabancılık duymama çekirdeği ile rahatlık veren kişi veya şey ve insana alışık hayvan gibi özelleşmiş biçimler ayrı katmanlarda tutulur; özel biçimler bütün dalı tanımlamaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişi ya da şey karşısında yabancılık, ürkme veya kaçınma duymayıp yakınlık, rahatlık ve sevinç hissetmeyi anlatır. Bu duyguyu veren kişi veya şeye ve insana alışık, saldırgan olmayan hayvana da aktarılır.

facets.statement: Bir kişi ya da şey karşısında yabancılık ve ürkme duygusunun kalkıp yakınlık, rahatlık veya sevinç oluşmasını anlatır.
Kişiye arkadaşlık ederek veya yanında bulunarak yabancılık duygusunu gideren kişi ya da şeyi adlandırır.
İnsana alışık ve saldırgan olmayan hayvanı, özellikle bu nitelikteki köpeği anlatabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak çekirdek, yabancılık ve kaçınmanın karşıtı olan yakınlık ve rahatlıktır. Bu durum birine alışıp onun yanında sevinmeyi, rahatlık veren kişi veya şeyi ve insana alışık saldırgan olmayan hayvanı kapsayacak biçimde genişler.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım çıplak dalın insana dönük yan çekirdeğiyle sınırlıdır. Hayvan ve yay uygulamaları bu çekirdeğin örneklenmesidir; yalnız bu kullanımlardan yeni bir genel yön anlamı çıkarılmaz.

Yayda okçuya doğru bakan ve kullanıcının karşısında bulunan yanı anlatır.
İnsana yakın yan bazı aktarımda sol, başka bir aktarımda sağ diye belirlenir; yönün özü bu değişken tanımlardan bağımsızdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak anlam, nesnenin insana veya kullanıcıya dönük yanıdır; hayvanda biniciye, yayda okçuya göre belirlenir. Geçici dal açıklamasındaki günler vurgusu kaynak ifadesinde açık değildir; bu nedenle dal korunmuş, fakat tanım yalnız kanıtlanan büyük meseleler ve dokunulmaz konular çevresinde yeniden kurulmuştur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam yalnız iki belirli üçlü anlatıma bağlıdır; genel olarak gün, ölüm, beden veya her büyük olay anlamına genişletilemez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal yalnız insan hayatındaki üç büyük mesele ile üç dokunulmaz konuyu bildiren iki sabit anlatımda tanıklanır; yalın anlam çıkarılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Belirli bir anlatımda insan hayatındaki üç büyük mesele veya dönüm noktasını, başka bir anlatımda ise çiğnendiği ya da dokunulmazlığı kaldırıldığı bildirilen üç önemli ve dokunulmaz konuyu belirtir. Anlam, bu iki üçlü anlatımın dışına taşmaz.

facets.statement: İnsan hayatına ilişkin üç büyük meseleyi veya dönüm noktasını bildiren sabit anlatımı belirtir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi tapınma eylemini, kişinin kendini tapınmaya vermesini, bir varlığı tapınılır kılmayı ve tapınılan varlığı aynı anlam örgüsü içinde açıkça birleştirir. Geçici dal çerçevesi bu çekirdeği ve ondan türeyen varlık adlarını doğru biçimde temsil eder.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, tapınma eylemi ile bundan türeyen tapınılan veya tapınılır kılınan varlık anlamlarını kapsar; şaşkınlık, yoğun üzüntü ve salt özel ad kullanımları bu sınırın dışındadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın eylem çekirdeğini türemiş eylem ve varlık adlarından ayırır; türemiş biçimlerin kapsamı yalın eylemin tamamına aktarılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir varlığa tapınma eylemini ve kişinin kendini tapınmaya vermesini anlatır. Türemiş kullanımlarda bir varlığı tapınılır kılmayı, tapınılan varlığı ve tapınma konusu sayılan varlıkları da adlandırır.

facets.statement: Temel eylem, bir varlığa tapınmak ve kişinin kendini bu tapınmaya vermesidir.
Eylemden türeyen varlık anlamı, kendisine tapınılan varlığı veya tapınma konusu sayılan nesneyi gösterir.
Ettirgen kullanım, bir varlığı başkalarınca tapınılır duruma getirme veya öyle sunma işlemini bildirir.
Güneşe kimi topluluklarca tapınılması nedeniyle ona tapınılan varlık anlamındaki bir ad verilmesi, varlık anlamının tarihsel bir örneğidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, tapınmayı anlamın temeli sayar; kişinin tapınmaya yönelmesini, tapınılan varlığı ve tapınılır kılma işlemini bu temelden türetir. Tapınma konusu sayılan yontular ve güneş örneği, varlık anlamının belirli uygulamalarıdır.

concept_gloss.text: tapınma ve tapınılan varlık

branches.source_phrase_ar: أصل واحد وهو التعبد، فالإله الله تعالى لأنه معبود، وتأله الرجل إذا تعبد، والإلاهة الشمس سميت بذلك لأن قوما كانوا يعبدونها (maqayis)؛ التأله التعبد (ayn)؛ أله بالفتح إلاهة أي عبد عبادة، مألوه أي معبود، الآلهة الأصنام، التأليه التعبيد، التأله التنسك والتعبد (sihah)؛ لا يكون إلاها حتى يكون معبودا، معبوداتهم من الأصنام والأوثان آلهة، الإلاهة الشمس، وإلاهتك وعبادتك (tahdhib)؛ إله اسما لكل معبود، أله فلان يأله الآلهة عبد، فالإله على هذا هو المعبود (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi Yaratıcıya özgü adın kendisini, genel tapınılan-varlık adından türetiliş açıklamasını ve bu özel adla kurulan seslenme ile ant biçimlerini birlikte verir. Geçici çerçeve kullanılabilir, ancak dal yalnızca seslenme ve ant kalıpları değildir; özel adın yalın kullanımı da çekirdekte tutulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, özel ad ile bu ada bağlı seslenme, dilek, şaşma ve ant biçimleriyle sınırlıdır; herhangi bir tapınılan varlığı gösteren genel ad anlamına genişletilmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın özel ad, doğrudan seslenme biçimleri ve ant ya da şaşma kalıpları ayrı tutulur; kalıplara özgü işlevler özel adın her kullanımına genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Yaratıcıya özgü adın kendisini ve bu adla kurulan seslenme, dilek, şaşma ve ant biçimlerini kapsar. Bu biçimler doğrudan seslenme, adın ant değeriyle kullanılması veya ses ve parçaların düşürülmesiyle kısaltılma yollarını gösterir.

facets.statement: Dalın merkezinde, Yaratıcıyı başkalarından ayırarak gösteren ve yalnız ona özgü sayılan özel ad bulunur.
Özel adın, tapınılan varlığı bildiren genel addan ses düşmesi ve belirleyici unsur eklenmesiyle oluştuğu açıklanır.
Özel ad, sözün başında ant değeri taşıyarak ardından gelen yapmama bildirimini güçlendirebilir.
Özel adın doğrudan ya da seslenme öğesi yerine geçen bir sonla kullanılması, yakarma ve dilek bildiren seslenme biçimleri kurar.
Ses veya parçaların düşürüldüğü kısalmış biçimler, şaşma ve ant anlatan kalıplarda kullanılır.
